text:
anna: Heads-up — canary on the sm95 pool showing a regression after last runtime tweak. p50 for seqlen=64 went from ~12ms -> ~19ms (1.6x).

raj: ugh. same model & batch config?

anna: yes, only runtime change was the new kernel routing heuristic + aggressive prefetch for kv cache when seqlen fluctuates.

mike: do we have profiler traces?

anna: pasted the lightweight trace from the canary node: 
```
RDW_PROBE: device=sm95 driver=537.21
kernel_pick: attention_fastpath_v3 (tensor=true, bf16=true)\nfallback: attention_scalar (tensor=false)
seqlen_dist: 1-32: 30%, 33-64: 55%, 65-128: 15%
kv_prefetch: enabled (hysteresis=0)
p50_tokens_ms: baseline=12.1 -> canary=19.0
trace: kernel_switch_count=18 prefetch_eviction=12
```

raj: kernel_switch_count=18 looks suspicious — we should not be flipping kernels mid-request. that likely thrashes L2 / kernel warmup.

lina: also prefetch_eviction=12 — KV cache thrash. if prefetch runs while seq pattern changes it evicts entries and subsequent requests miss.

mike: where's the capability probe output? maybe device flags are wrong and we hit a scalar fallback for some micro-batches.

anna: probe output from runtime discovery: 
```
{"gpu_sm":95, "tensor_cores":true, "bf16_hw":true, "fp8_hw":false, "cap_flags": ["sm95","tc","bf16"]}
```

raj: hmm fp8_hw=false but cap_flags doesn't include fp8 — ok. any mismatch between reported tc/bf16 and kernel runtime check?

anna: digging deeper, the kernel selection logs show a path where we require both tc && bf16 to pick attention_fastpath_v3, but a second probe (lazy) reported tc=true but bf16=false for some GPUs during warmup which forced fallback until bf16 was reinitialized. that explains kernel_switch_count.

mike: that could be a race in the capability cache population. if early requests see inconsistent capabilities we toggle picks. need to make capability detection idempotent and stable.

lina: operational suggestion: add a short hysteresis window before switching kernel on a per-device basis (e.g., require N consistent probes or >X% of last M requests indicating capability) + only allow kernel switches between requests, not during an in-flight batch.

raj: agree. also we should gate prefetch behavior with sequence-length hysteresis. current prefetch enabled for any seqlen>32 instantly; change to enable only when >32 for 5 consecutive requests or mean seqlen over 1s >32.

anna: i ran a micro-experiment: patched hysteresis=3 (3 consistent probes) + prefetch_stability=5. reran canary on single node — p50 back to ~13.2ms, kernel_switch_count down to 1, prefetch_eviction=0.

mike: nice. can you paste the exact patch snippet you used?

anna: snippet in runtime knobs: 
```
# gating config
seqlen_prefetch_threshold = 32
seqlen_prefetch_stability = 5  # require 5 successive samples
cap_probe_consistency = 3     # require 3 consistent capability samples
allow_kernel_switch_inflight = false
```

lina: small follow-ups: instrument metrics for "kernel_switch_count" and "cap_probe_inconsistency" with per-device tags. we need heatmaps to catch this earlier.

raj: create a regression test in perf CI that simulates jittered seqlen distribution and verifies p50 doesn't regress >1.2x.

ci-bot: perf run queued: https://ci.internal/perf/4123456789 (run id 98765) — target: canary-sm95, seqlen-mix test.

anna: i'll open an issue with repro, the patch, and the perf run link. assigning to @mike to review kernel switching code and @raj to add CI test.

mike: ack, I'll take kernel review. planning to add unit tests for probe stabilization and ensure the capability cache write is atomic.

raj: I'll add the perf test and a dashboard panel for kernel_switch_count.

lina: i'll add KV cache eviction metric and a quick alert if prefetch_eviction > 1% of requests for >1m.

anna: thanks. experiment shows the heuristic fixes the canary — will promote patch after PR reviews. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: perf run completed: https://ci.internal/perf/4123456789/results — p50=13.3ms, kernel_switch_count=1, prefetch_eviction=0 — regression resolved on test node.

mike: LGTM. we'll roll the hysteresis change to the canary pool and monitor.

lina: note for release notes: "runtime: add capability probe stability and prefetch seqlen hysteresis to reduce kernel thrash and KV cache evictions on jittery workloads."

anna: closing this thread after PR merged. will follow up if other anomalies crop up.
